title: Daily range partitions for recon.fact_leg and recon.break_header
subtitle: Postgres 13. Partition by settlement_date, not hash. Detach after 400 days. Lock budget 8 seconds. Fix recon-query so it stops filtering created_at if it wants exclusion.
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Rina Das (DBA), Priya Nair, Kavya Menon, Chris Patel, Diego Alvarez, Helen Cho
owners: Aman Kumar (design), Rina Das (migration window), Kavya Menon (recon-query changes)
related: CLH-TDD-2022-021, CLH-MEM-2023-004, CLH-2104, NS-DBA-118, CLH-2441 (autovacuum catch-up), CLH-TDD-2023-008
summary: recon.fact_leg is 1.84 TB, unpartitioned, and month-end inserts peaked at 8.2M rows in a 4.7 hour window on April 28. Autovacuum on that table held a snapshot long enough that match-engine write latency hit 12.4 seconds p95 (CLH-2441). This design range-partitions fact_leg and break_header by settlement_date, daily, on Postgres 13. We detach partitions older than 400 days to the cold tablespace tbs_recon_cold. Hash partitioning is rejected because every query Helen and Chris run is a date range. The lock budget for the cutover is 8 seconds. recon-query currently predicates on created_at, which will miss constraint exclusion, and Kavya has to change that before we cut.
form_description: Technical design for range-partitioning Clearhaven recon fact and break tables in Postgres 13, including indexes, detach-to-cold, query-planner risks, and an 8-second lock-budget migration.
revision_history: Notes from Rina after CLH-2441. Hash vs range argument started here.
Added lock-budget rehearsal numbers from pg-recon-dev clone.
Corrected default tablespace names. Insisted on UNIQUE including settlement_date.
Priya approved. recon-query created_at issue called out as a hard gate.

blocks.text: Purpose

This is the design Rina Das and I will execute against pg-recon-01.prod.nseng.internal, Postgres 13.11, database recon. Two tables: recon.fact_leg and recon.break_header. Both grow by settlement day and both are queried by settlement day. Neither is partitioned. Vacuum, index bloat, and the April 28 8.2M insert spike are the reasons we are doing this now rather than after the Kafka cutover lands in a quieter week. Priya asked for a design she can send to Marcus if Clearhaven's own DBA, Nate Okonkwo, wants to read it. Nate does not operate this cluster. Rina does. Nate still gets a copy.

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: RANGE partition both tables by settlement_date (daily). Primary key and unique constraints include settlement_date. Create 14 days of future partitions via cron. Detach partitions with settlement_date < current_date - 400 and move them to tbs_recon_cold. Do not hash-partition. Do not list-partition by account prefix. recon-query must predicate settlement_date before we cut, or the planner will scan every daily partition and we will have paid for nothing.
Constraints we are not negotiating

items: Postgres 13.11. No native PK on the parent without the partition key. We will not upgrade to 14 this year; Diego already said the major upgrade is a 2024 item.
Lock budget 8 seconds on the rename/swap. Helen's matcher writes continuously from 14:05 to 19:35 ET. A 30-second ACCESS EXCLUSIVE is a missed cycle and a page.
Peak insert 8.2M rows in 4.7 hours (April 28 month-end). Typical weekday 1.36M. Weekend 0 (we do not settle). The partition scheme has to survive 8.2M, not 1.36M.
Helen and the desk query by settlement_date. Chris's Tableau extracts filter settlement_date BETWEEN. match-engine lookups are settlement_date = $1 AND account_no = $2.
400-day online retention. Compliance (Maya Singh, not in this meeting) said 7 years in cold storage. Cold is still Postgres, different tablespace, cheaper disks, not S3 yet.
Zero application downtime is the wish. 8 seconds of blocked writes is the budget. If the rehearsal on the clone exceeds 8 seconds we change the method, we do not 'try it in prod and see.'

blocks.text: Current shape

recon.fact_leg has 487 million rows, 1.84 TB including indexes, fillfactor 100, last successful autovacuum April 28 23:11 which is 4 hours after the spike, which is how we got CLH-2441. Live indexes: pk_fact_leg on (leg_id), uq_fact_leg_natural on (account_no, cusip, settle_date, source_ref), ix_fact_leg_settle on (settlement_date), ix_fact_leg_created on (created_at), ix_fact_leg_acct_settle on (account_no, settlement_date). Yes, settle_date and settlement_date are both on this table. settle_date is a leftover text column from the CSV parser. settlement_date is date, not null, and is what match-engine uses. We partition on settlement_date. We do not partition on settle_date. I will not rename the text column in this project.

recon.break_header has 61.4 million rows, 214 GB, PK on break_id, ix_break_settle on (settlement_date, status), ix_break_created on (created_at). Helen's queue is 'open breaks for settlement_date = today and yesterday.' Chris's aging report is last 90 days. Nobody has asked for a break by created_at except recon-query's default dashboard, which Kavya copied from an early prototype and which is the landmine in this design.

blocks.caption: Table stats from pg-recon-01, snapshot May 12 09:14 ET, Rina's monitoring role.

blocks.text: match_result is larger. We are not partitioning it in this change. Rina wants one painful migration, not two, and match_result is append-mostly with a 90-day purge Kavya already cronned. fact_leg and break_header are the ones vacuum cannot keep up with and the ones whose indexes Helen waits on during the 18:40 catch-up. If this goes well, match_result is a Q4 design. If this goes badly, we do not touch match_result this year.
Rejected: hash partitioning

Chris asked, because 8.2M inserts into one daily partition still looks like a hot partition. Hash on account_no into 32 partitions would spread the write. It would also make every date-range query touch 32 children unless we always include account_no, which Helen's queue does not. Constraint exclusion on hash partitions in PG 13 is not a date prune. We would be buying write spread and paying it back on the only queries that matter. Rina ran EXPLAIN on a 90-day aging query against a hashed clone of 40 days of data. 32 workers, 18.4 seconds, vs 1.9 seconds on the same data range-partitioned by day with the date predicate. That is the whole argument.

blocks.label: Rejected: hash on account_no
blocks.text: Workload is range queries by settlement_date. Hash does not prune those. PG 13 hash partitions also make the 400-day detach story messy (you detach a hash child that still holds hot dates). Do not 'hash and also range' as a composite in this version. Composite is a PG 11+ feature we could use later; it doubles the partition count and Rina does not want 32 x 400 children until we prove daily range is boring.

List partitioning by account prefix died faster. Clearhaven account_no is not a stable prefix scheme (introducing broker codes got reused in 2019). I am not encoding a 2019 business rule into the storage layout.
Target layout

Parent tables named as today. Children named fact_leg_pYYYYMMDD and break_header_pYYYYMMDD, CHECK implied by FOR VALUES FROM (d) TO (d+1). Default partition fact_leg_pdefault / break_header_pdefault exists so a mis-dated row does not fail the insert, it lands in default and pages us. Default should stay near empty. If it is not empty we have a producer writing settlement_date outside the 14-day future window, which is a bug, not a storage feature.

blocks.caption: Parent and one child. Run in a transaction on the clone first. Do not run this as-is on prod; the migration section is the prod path.
blocks.text:
-- fact_leg parent (illustrative). Prod path uses rename-and-attach, see below.
CREATE TABLE recon.fact_leg_new (
    leg_id           bigserial,
    account_no       text        NOT NULL,
    cusip            text        NOT NULL,
    settle_date      text,
    settlement_date  date        NOT NULL,
    source_ref       text        NOT NULL,
    qty              numeric(18,4) NOT NULL,
    side             char(1)     NOT NULL,
    net_amt          numeric(18,4),
    executing_broker text,
    ingest_source    text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'drop',
    bus_offset       bigint,
    created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (leg_id, settlement_date),
    UNIQUE (account_no, cusip, settlement_date, source_ref)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (settlement_date);

CREATE TABLE recon.fact_leg_p20230518
    PARTITION OF recon.fact_leg_new
    FOR VALUES FROM ('2023-05-18') TO ('2023-05-19');

CREATE INDEX ix_fact_leg_p20230518_acct
    ON recon.fact_leg_p20230518 (account_no, settlement_date);
CREATE INDEX ix_fact_leg_p20230518_created
    ON recon.fact_leg_p20230518 (created_at);

-- default catch-all; alert if row_count > 0 for 15 minutes
CREATE TABLE recon.fact_leg_pdefault
    PARTITION OF recon.fact_leg_new DEFAULT;
Why the PK includes settlement_date

PG 13 requires unique constraints on partitioned tables to include the partition key. leg_id is a bigserial and is unique on its own today. After partition, PRIMARY KEY (leg_id) is illegal. PRIMARY KEY (leg_id, settlement_date) is legal and is still unique in practice because leg_id is global. break-svc and two Tableau extracts join on leg_id only. Those joins still work. They cannot use the PK as a single-column lookup and will seq-scan a partition if we do not keep a secondary unique index on (leg_id, settlement_date) which the PK already is, or a global uniqueness story we do not have. A duplicate leg_id across two days cannot happen with bigserial. I am not building a trigger to police it. Nate asked. Rina said no.
Indexes per child

We do not create indexes on the parent and hope. On PG 13, CREATE INDEX on the parent fans out, which is what we want for new children, and we will CREATE INDEX on the parent after children exist so they all get ix_fact_leg_acct (account_no, settlement_date), ix_fact_leg_created (created_at), ix_fact_leg_source (ingest_source, settlement_date). The natural UNIQUE stays. We drop ix_fact_leg_settle on (settlement_date) because a single-column date index on a daily partition is a waste; every row in the child has the same date. That drop is the one Rina is happiest about. 0.72 TB of indexes on fact_leg includes a lot of that date index.

rows: Support recon-query until Kavya removes it, then drop

blocks.text: Constraint exclusion and the recon-query trap

PG 13 still uses constraint exclusion / partition pruning. If the query has settlement_date = '2023-05-18' or a range the planner can see at plan time, it opens one or N children and ignores the rest. If the query filters created_at BETWEEN now() - interval '2 days' AND now(), the planner cannot prove which children apply, because created_at is not the partition key and a row created today can have settlement_date of yesterday (we see that on late drops and on bus replay). Result: every daily partition is scanned, 400 of them after a year, and we will have made the dashboard slower than the unpartitioned table. I reproduced this on the clone. 412 partitions, predicate on created_at only: 28.6 seconds. Same query with settlement_date >= current_date - 2: 0.41 seconds.

recon-query is the Go service behind Helen's 'recent activity' panel. Kavya wrote it in October. The default filter is created_at. There is no settlement_date in the query string unless the user picks a date on the advanced form, which Helen does not, because the default looks like it works. It works today because there is one heap. After partition it will still return correct rows and it will do it the expensive way. This is a hard gate. Kavya changes the default predicate to settlement_date >= current_date - 2 OR (status = 'OPEN') with settlement_date on the open-break index path. Chris's Tableau extracts already pass settlement_date. match-engine already passes it. The gap is recon-query and one ad-hoc script in Helen's home directory on ops-bastion-02 that she will not let me see. I will sit with her and rewrite the script before cutover.

blocks.label: Gate: recon-query
blocks.text: Do not cut over while recon-query's default WHERE is created_at only. Ship Kavya's change, watch EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) in prod for 48 hours against the still-unpartitioned table (the predicate change is valid today), then migrate. If we reverse the order, Helen's panel is the pager.
400-day detach to cold

tbs_recon_cold is a tablespace on the gp3 volume rina attached in April, 4 TB, 3000 IOPS, cheaper than the io2 volume the hot heap lives on. Detach is ALTER TABLE ... DETACH PARTITION ... CONCURRENTLY, which PG 13.11 has (it landed in 13, we confirmed on the clone). CONCURRENTLY still takes a short ACCESS EXCLUSIVE at the end. On the clone that final lock was 0.4-1.1 seconds per partition with no traffic. With replayed match-engine traffic it was 1.8-3.2 seconds. Under 8. Fine. After detach we ALTER TABLE fact_leg_pYYYYMMDD SET TABLESPACE tbs_recon_cold, which copies the relation and is IO-heavy, so we do that at 22:30 ET, not during the window. Then we DROP INDEX ix_created and ix_source on the detached table. Queries against cold go through a union view recon.fact_leg_all that Rina will own. Application code does not use the union. Only Chris's 13-month lookback and Maya's audit extract do.

Job: recon-partman, a CronJob at 00:25 ET, creates next 14 daily children if missing, detaches children with upper bound < current_date - 400, notifies #clh-recon with the list. If create fails we page, because tomorrow's inserts would land in default. If detach fails we page at warning, not page-page, because the only cost is the hot volume staying fatter. Diego wires the CronJob. Rina owns the SQL functions. I review the first two weeks of logs.

blocks.caption: Detach and cold move. recon-partman calls this per aged child. 22:30 ET only for SET TABLESPACE.

blocks.text: Migration plan (lock budget 8 seconds)

We will not CLUSTER, we will not rewrite 1.84 TB in a maintenance window Helen does not have. Method: pg_partman-style swap used on the clone. Build a partitioned parent alongside, backfill children from the old heap by settlement_date in 7-day chunks with INSERT SELECT, keep a trigger on the old heap that duplicates writes into the new parent during backfill, then in a single transaction rename old to fact_leg_legacy, rename new to fact_leg, drop the trigger. The rename transaction is the 8-second budget. Everything else is online.

items: T-14 days: Kavya ships recon-query predicate change. Helen's script rewritten. EXPLAIN captured for match-engine lookup, recon-query default, Chris 90-day extract. Gate review with Rina and Priya.

T-10 days: Create fact_leg_new / break_header_new partitioned, empty, indexes on parent. Create children for settlement_date from current_date - 30 through current_date + 14. Older history is a second phase; see below.

T-10 to T-2: Backfill last 30 days with INSERT INTO fact_leg_new SELECT ... WHERE settlement_date = $day, one day at a time, 4 workers, during 20:00-23:30 ET. April 28-shaped days took 38 minutes on the clone for 8.2M rows. Watch WAL; Diego throttles if replica lag on pg-recon-01-repl > 12 seconds.

T-10: Install recon.tg_fact_leg_dual fire ON INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE on fact_leg, writing the same row to fact_leg_new. This is the ugly part. Trigger cost on the clone was +0.7 ms per insert at 3.1k rows/s. match-engine p95 write went from 9.4 ms to 11.1 ms. Acceptable. If prod shows worse than +3 ms p95 we abort and drop the trigger.

T-2: Catch up any rows the day-batch missed (trigger should have them; we still run a checksum of counts and max(leg_id) per settlement_date). Chris builds recon.part_checksum for this. Divergence must be 0.

T-0, 10:05 ET Tuesday (not a month-end, not a settlement Monday). Change ticket NS-CHG-2023-188. Priya or backup signer (Rahul is not a signer; Diego is backup if Priya is out). Helen on Zoom. Freeze match-engine deploys.

T-0 cutover transaction: stop the dual-write trigger, lock both tables, rename, grant, commit. Rehearsal on clone with replayed writes: 4.6 to 7.1 seconds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. If the prod attempt hits 7 seconds we still proceed. If we abort at 8, the transaction rolls back and we are on the old heap. There is no half-rename.

T+0 to T+2 hours: watch insert errors, default partition row_count, match-engine p95, recon-query p95. Rollback is rename back, which is another 8-second lock. We only rollback for wrong results or default partition filling, not for a slow dashboard.

T+1 day through T+21: backfill settlement_date older than 30 days into dated children, 7-day chunks, 22:30 ET, no trigger needed because those days are not receiving inserts. When a historical day is in a child, we can DETACH that slice from consideration in the legacy heap by deleting from fact_leg_legacy. We drop fact_leg_legacy only when Chris signs the 400-day checksum.

blocks.text: The 30-day hot backfill plus trigger plus rename is how we keep the lock tiny. The 400-day history backfill is slow and boring and can slip a week without Helen noticing. I am not combining them into one insert. Rina wanted that said in writing because the last time someone 'just copied the table' on this cluster it was 2019 and it took the replica down.

blocks.caption: Cutover transaction. Rehearse with pg_stat_activity sampled every 200ms. Abort if wait_event is LockManager past 8s (application-side cancel).

blocks.text: Failure modes

lock_timeout fires at 8 seconds. Transaction rolls back. Old names remain. Trigger is gone, so for the seconds after abort we are not dual-writing. The runbook says recreate the trigger immediately if we abort, then go home, do not retry the same morning. Retry is the next Tuesday. I would rather lose a week than hold ACCESS EXCLUSIVE while match-engine queues 200k writes.

Inserts land in fact_leg_pdefault because recon-partman failed to create tomorrow. Alert on n_live_tup of pdefault > 0. Page Rina and me. Fix is create the missing child, INSERT SELECT from default, delete from default. Do this before the next match cycle if we can. If we cannot, default is still a heap the parent will scan. Ugly, correct.

A query without settlement_date hits 400 children. We will find these by pg_stat_statements after cutover, ordered by shared_blks_hit, Rina already has a saved query. First week I am on the hook to patch callers. Known remaining risk: the Metabase card 'legs by broker' that someone on Marcus's side created with a personal account. We cannot see it until it runs. If it runs at 10:00 and takes 4 minutes we live. If it runs at 18:10 and takes 4 minutes we kill it and talk to Marcus.

DETACH CONCURRENTLY deadlocks with a long reporting query. PG 13 will wait. Our CronJob has a 120-second statement_timeout on detach. Failed detach retries next night. Do not DETACH during 14:05-19:35. The job is 00:25 for a reason. If someone runs it by hand at 16:00 I will be unkind.

Unique violation on (account_no, cusip, settlement_date, source_ref) during backfill if the trigger and the day-batch both insert. The day-batch uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. The trigger uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. If you write a backfill without that, you will stop the job at 18% and ping me. The SQL in tools/part_backfill.sql has it. Copy that, not your memory.
What this does to Kafka ingest

CLH-MEM-2023-004 is turning the 15-minute lump into a trickle. That is good for a daily partition: writes spread across the afternoon instead of arriving as 180k-row bursts every 15 minutes. It does not change the partition key. It does change autovacuum timing on today's child, which Rina will retune (scale_factor 0.02 on children, not 0.2). I am not packing vacuum tuning into the cutover. She gets a week of data first.
